candidates.priority: high, if selected as a narrow measurement-design lemma
candidates.exactQuestion: For a real symmetric positive-definite two-coordinate stiffness matrix with known calibrated masses and signed coordinate conventions, which of two modal frequencies, one diagonal static compliance and one signed cross compliance determine the stiffness matrix?
candidates.baselineAlreadyDone: Common stiffness/density scaling and a selected calibrated static discriminator; partial-resolvent noninjectivity countermodel.
candidates.distinctNewObjective: Establish sufficiency and a precise remaining ambiguity for a specified finite measurement set; do not just repeat the known scale symmetry.
premises: Mass-normalize coordinates using known positive masses.
K is a real symmetric positive-definite 2x2 matrix.
Mode labels, signed force/displacement ports and compliance calibration are known.
Static compliance is K inverse; no hidden modes, unknown supports or nonlinear terms.
hypothesisLedger: No external inverse-elasticity theorem is needed.
If sensor orientation is unknown, sign-related matrices may be coordinate-equivalent: report that equivalence, not a new physical ambiguity.
candidates.proposedProofOrTest: Use trace/determinant from squared modal frequencies and exact inverse-matrix entries; prove the admitted sufficiency statement and construct alternatives when an observable is omitted.
candidates.positiveControl: A nonsingular SPD matrix reconstructed from its exact declared measurements.
candidates.decisiveCountercontrol: K+=[[2,1],[1,3]] and K-=[[2,-1],[-1,3]] have the same frequencies and diagonal compliance but opposite signed cross compliance. Preserve or quotient the sign convention explicitly.
evidenceRequiredForAcceptance: Exact algebraic proof on the declared domain.
Independent review of omitted-observable and sign-convention controls.
State separately that exact identification does not establish conditioning under noise.
candidates.noveltyLabel: Known finite linear algebra applied to project measurement design; no novel inverse theorem claim.

resourcesAndPrerequisites.estimate: 4-8 agent-hours including independent mathematical review; negligible compute; no instrument requirement
resourcesAndPrerequisites.prerequisite: Advisor freezes exact observation set and coordinate conventions.

candidates.independentReview: A reviewer specifies indistinguishable pairs before seeing any producer reconstruction code.
candidates.stopRule: Stop after proof/counterexample for this 2x2 contract; if calibration is unknown, classify the equivalence class instead of widening the claim. No continuum or full-spectrum extension.

candidates.priority: high before any complete-cycle energy wording
candidates.exactQuestion: Can the proposed cycle ledger reject a claimed reset that restores subsystem marginals while consuming joint correlations or another omitted resource?
candidates.baselineAlreadyDone: Signed heat in a single fixed-H thermal channel, passive energy versus ergotropy, and ideal reservoir dilation.
candidates.distinctNewObjective: Define and test cycle closure for joint states/resources rather than equating local energy closure with a reusable apparatus cycle.
premises: Explicit noninteracting reference Hamiltonian for the states being compared, with interaction off at cycle endpoints.
List system, finite reservoir, controller/memory and work-storage states or explicitly mark unmodeled resources.
Work accessibility and reset implementation are not assumed costless.
hypothesisLedger: The identity F(rho_AB)-F(rho_A tensor rho_B)=k_B*T*I(A:B) is a resource-accounting identity for additive H, not by itself an achievable-work theorem.
Any reset/work bound requires a separately named operational class and exact theorem hypotheses.
candidates.proposedProofOrTest: Prepare a finite ledger specification distinguishing joint-state reset, marginal reset, energy closure and implementation cost; independently verify one correlated-state countercontrol and a genuine product-state closure control.
candidates.positiveControl: Identical initial and final product state with identical endpoint Hamiltonian and all declared resource accounts restored.
candidates.decisiveCountercontrol: A classically correlated diagonal two-qubit state with probabilities (1-nu,0,0,nu) and its product of marginals share local populations and additive energy but differ in joint entropy and correlation free energy, for 0<nu<1.
evidenceRequiredForAcceptance: The ledger refuses an unconditional reusable-cycle label when joint correlations, control, memory or reset costs remain unmodeled.
Any computed work bound is explicitly conditional on the declared operations.
No modeled gain is described as source-free energy.
candidates.noveltyLabel: A project accounting specification and established-information-theory control, not a new energy source or thermodynamic theorem.

resourcesAndPrerequisites.estimate: 6-12 agent-hours for specification, exact two-qubit derivation and independent review; small matrices only
resourcesAndPrerequisites.prerequisite: Choose one complete idealized cycle and operational boundary first; otherwise park after specification.

candidates.independentReview: Separate reviewer checks global-state and Hamiltonian endpoint conditions before accepting the cycle label.
candidates.stopRule: If no complete operational cycle can be specified within the cap, return missing-resource obligations. Do not infer apparatus efficiency or enlarge the task into unrestricted quantum thermodynamics.
limits: No blanket achievable-work assertion from mutual information.
No implementation or experiment performed in this review.
